title: Integration weekly snapshot - TigerBridge onboarding
content:
Meeting: Solutions Eng + ProServices weekly sync (TigerBridge onboarding)
Date: 2028-02-14 10:30am PT
Location: Zoom / #se-proservices Slack thread
Attendees: Jordan Kim, Aisha Patel, Diego Morales, Priya Shah, Product Ops (Lena Ortiz), TigerBridge technical lead (call-in at 11am PT)

SUMMARY:
- Focus this week: stabilize model routing under heavy burst traffic and unblock customer schema mapping for their webhooks ingestion pipeline.
- Short-term SLA risk: observed 3x latency spike during prefix-cache churn in canary; currently mitigated by temporary routing to smaller-quantized model variant. Need permanent fix before full ramp.

CUSTOMER STATUS (TigerBridge):
- Onboarding phase: validation -> 50% of test traffic routed to assigned dedicated pool.
- Integration acceptance criteria: end-to-end throughput 120 rps sustained, p95 latency < 180ms for short prompts, successful webhook forwarding with schema v2 fields present.
- Today: webhook schema mismatch still failing 12% of messages (field mapping mismatch for `session_id`).

TECHNICAL UPDATES:
- Runtime / Serving: Diego observed KV cache eviction thrash when many short-lived sessions come in (bursty onboarding tests). Root cause: cache key length mis-hash when sessions exceed 10k TTL churn. Patch proposed: change hash namespace -> PR created.
  - PR: https://github.com/redwood/infra/pull/412 (Diego)
  - Risk: needs e2e canary before merging; potential small memory footprint increase.
- Model routing: temporary fallback to quantized-x72 variant reduced token cost but raised p95 by ~30ms on long prompts. Config change applied in routing policy for TigerBridge tenant to prefer low-latency nodes (policy token: tenant:TIGERBRIDGE/latency-priority).
- Data plane: webhook processor mapping rules currently drop `session_id` when payload contains nested `metadata` arrays. Product Ops provided sample payloads; engineering needs deterministic mapping rules.

BLOCKERS / RISKS:
- Blocker-1: Schema mapping ambiguity for `session_id` (customer uses both top-level and nested field depending on platform version). Without a robust fallback we risk 12–20% message loss on ramp. Owner: Priya Shah.
- Blocker-2: KV cache hotkey eviction causing transient latency spikes under synthetic load. Requires a runtime patch + canary (Diego).
- Escalation: If patch cannot be validated by 2028-02-21, temporarily extend fallback routing (costly) and push a slowed ramp to TigerBridge.

ACTIONS (owner / ETA):
- Priya Shah: implement tolerant mapping rule that looks for `session_id` in top-level and in `payload.metadata[*].session_id`, return canonical field; add unit tests. ETA: 2028-02-17.
- Diego Morales: finalize hash-namespace change, submit canary config, run 24h burst test. ETA: canary start 2028-02-16, results by 2028-02-17.
- Aisha Patel: coordinate with TigerBridge SRE for a controlled ramp test window Friday 2/18 09:00–11:00 PT; collect live traces. ETA: confirm by EOD 2/14.
- Jordan Kim: update routing policy to set temporary conservative capacity headroom and create rollback playbook. ETA: 2028-02-15.
- Lena Ortiz (Product Ops): consolidate sample webhook payload variants into a single test corpus and upload to shared bucket: gs://redwood-integrations/tigerbridge/test-corpus. ETA: 2028-02-16.

DECISIONS MADE:
- We will keep fallback to quantized-x72 model for non-critical routes until KV patch is validated. Fallback will be removed only after 24h of stable canary results.
- Mapping code path will prioritize explicit top-level `session_id` then nested; ambiguous messages will be logged and queued for manual review instead of dropped.

NOTES / ASIDE (informal):
- Priya: "customer has a legacy connector that sometimes injects arrays for metadata — we should add a small adapter in the webhook layer to normalize shapes."
- Diego: observed small memory bump with hash-namespace; likely acceptable at current Dedicated pool sizes but monitor.

OPEN QUESTIONS:
- Do we want to add a temporary synthetic traffic guard in the router to limit short-burst concurrency per session id? (Pros: reduces KV churn; Cons: could throttle legitimate spikes.)
- Can SRE provide a JVM/OS-level snapshot during the next canary run to help correlate GC/memory with eviction events?

FOLLOW-UPS FOR NEXT MEETING (2028-02-21):
- Canaries: results + traces (Diego)
- Schema mapping test results (Priya)
- Customer feedback + ramp schedule (Aisha + TigerBridge)
- Cost impact estimate for continued fallback routing (Jordan + Finance contact)

QUICK TODOS (personal notes):
- Jordan: prepare rollback runbook and share in #se-proservices by EOD 2/15.
- Priya: add logging flags to capture ambiguous payloads without PII.
- Diego: instrument eviction counters at finer granularity (per-shard).

DOCUMENT HISTORY / CONTEXT:
- Related tickets: JIRA-7832 (webhook mapping), JIRA-7891 (KV cache eviction).
- Previous action: routing policy change applied 2028-02-12 as hotfix for immediate latency relief.

END OF NOTES

Parking lot (items to drop into backlog):
- Investigate adaptive per-tenant cache sizing.
- Small adapter library for common legacy connector shapes (might become a product add-on).

-- Jordan
